executive_summary:
In the window from 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-22, ARI3 collected 4,250 raw source records from 78 outlet domains. Final signal evidence was deduplicated so exact mirrors and syndicated or translated versions of the same publication count as one report evidence unit. The editor retained 20 signals. The largest by item count are sneaker (53 items from 12 outlets), denim (24 from 16) and vintage (20 from 16). Sneaker is concentrated, with 25 of its items from two outlets, and Mary Jane sneakers and 1990s styles recur within it. Denim and vintage are widely spread: denim leans on party-season coverage, and vintage on celebrity and royal dressing.

Loafer (11 items from 7 outlets) centres on one BEAMS and adidas loafer, tailoring (11 from 11) appears one item per outlet, and minimalism has 11 items from 9 outlets. Burgundy, trench, streetwear and suede have 6 to 9 items each. The smaller clusters, with 2 to 4 items, are Gen Z, Mary Jane, wide-leg, bomber, leather jacket, leopard, maximalism, oversized, ballet flat and barrel leg. These are patterns in the sources ARI3 collects, which were 89.7% editorial in this window. They do not measure consumer adoption or what people wear.

Mary Jane sneakers from adidas and Nike recur. Princess Diana's Superga sneakers at auction and a guide for readers over sneakers complete the set.

limitations: Items are counted as style only when the ARI3 style classifier (frozen v0.0.2) gives a confident yes. On a 150-item prospective holdout of articles published after the classifier was frozen, its accuracy was 0.833, below its pre-registered 0.85 criterion (EXP-003A, H2 not supported). The editor reviews every evidence item used in this report.
In this window, 1,961 of 4,250 items (46.1%) received a not-sure prediction set and were excluded from style-positive counts.

In this window, 89.7% of collected items came from the editorial sector and 95.4% from the editorial group (editorial, trade intelligence and independent criticism). The stored corpus as a whole is 89.4% editorial sector.

The window has 0 items from social platforms, which are not collected, and 4 from resale sources. The report describes the language of the collected sources, not style culture, fashion consumers or the public at large.
Signal interpretation and evidence review are done by one editor.
ARI3 stores each item's headline and feed excerpt, not the full article.
0 of the window's 4250 items were stored before 2026-09-30, so their first-seen times are reconstructed from earlier records, not recorded as they happened.
Seven ambiguous lexicon terms (western, brat, demure, lace, bow, sustainable, glamour) are left out of every count until their uses are checked one by one.

Exact mirrors and syndicated, translated or lightly re-edited versions of the same publication across publisher domains are collapsed to one report evidence unit. The frozen source snapshot retains the raw records.
ai_assistance: ARI3’s deterministic pipeline surfaced candidate signals and bound the report to a frozen evidence snapshot. An AI assistant drafted the executive summary, evidence text, and index notes using only the locked report evidence, including translations of non-English headlines. The editor selected and merged signals, set labels and confidence overrides, pruned evidence, reviewed the drafted text, wrote the editor notes, and approved the final report.
headline: Denim leaned on party-season coverage and vintage on celebrity and royal dressing
